When comparing PostgreSQL pgvector with Pinecone for vector search:

You CANNOT include GPLv3 code inside an Apache 2.0 project if the resulting project is to be distributed under Apache 2.0. goldens.input: Explain the architectural differences, memory footprint, and recall trade-offs between HNSW and IVFFlat vector indexing algorithms.

search_results.title: Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) Indexing In-Depth - Pinecone Learning
search_results.content: HNSW constructs a multi-layer graph where bottom layers contain all vectors and top layers contain long-range skip links. It achieves outstanding query recall (>98%) with sub-millisecond search latencies. However, its memory overhead is high (1.5x to 2x raw vector size) because all graph link pointers must remain in RAM, and building the index is computationally intensive.

search_results.title: Inverted File Flat (IVFFlat) Partitioning Trade-offs - Faiss Architecture Wiki
search_results.content: IVFFlat partitions the vector space into Voronoi cells using k-means clustering and searches only the centroids closest to the query (controlled by `nprobe`). It requires zero graph overhead (minimal RAM beyond raw vectors) and builds rapidly. The trade-off is lower peak recall (typically 80-92% depending on `nprobe`) and search speed degrades as `nprobe` increases.

IVFFlat partitions the vector space into Voronoi cells using k-means clustering and searches only the centroids closest to the query (controlled by `nprobe`). goldens.expected_output:
The architectural differences and trade-offs between HNSW and IVFFlat are:

- **HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World)** [1]:
  - **Structure**: Multi-layer graph with skip links between hierarchical layers.
  - **Recall & Speed**: Delivers high recall (>98%) and sub-millisecond search speeds.
  - **Trade-offs**: High memory footprint (1.5x to 2x vector size in RAM for graph pointers) and slow, resource-heavy index build times.
- **IVFFlat (Inverted File Flat)** [2]:
  - **Structure**: Inverted file partitioning using k-means clustering into Voronoi cells, queried via `nprobe`.
  - **Memory & Build**: Minimal RAM overhead (near raw vector size) and very fast index creation.
  - **Trade-offs**: Lower recall (80-92%) and increased query latency when scanning higher numbers of centroids (`nprobe`).
